sources.note: Shows that reasoning ability can be incentivized in an LLM by pure reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks, with no human-annotated reasoning trajectories, and that the resulting reasoning patterns can be transferred to smaller models.
sources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Inserts optimizable latent states at an intermediate Transformer layer rather than at the output, so self-attention makes every continuation token's log-probability differentiable with respect to every latent and reward-weighted gradients reach them from the whole continuation instead of only through their own decoded token.
sources.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning

sources.note: Separates hallucination into a reasoning failure and a knowledge failure, treats the first with a structured reflect-before-answering format and the second with a reward for abstaining when no sampled chain succeeds, and shows the two mechanisms are not interchangeable -- reflection alone never abstains, abstention alone never lowers the hallucination proxy.
sources.title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment

sources.note: Injects a retrieved solved problem, with its full worked solution, into the middle of a reasoning model's own thinking trace at each step boundary, using the model's current intermediate answer as the retrieval query.
sources.title: ThinkRetrieve: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Traces for Test-Time Scaling

sources.note: Adds a Self-Reflection token that lets reasoning models recover from harmful output mid-generation, cutting harmful completion rate from 13.8% to 4.1%.
sources.title: Self-Reflection Improves Safety of Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
sources.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

result.definition: Prompting or training a model to review its own output before committing, and across 6 sources a mechanism whose reported benefits the archive holds alongside two deflating measurements. The deflations: the precision of emergent self-corrections is measured at 24.4 percent, and reinforcement learning largely preserves the base model's existing entropy structure rather than installing a new reflective one -- so the 'emergent self-reflection' framing is not supported by the archive's own material. A qualitative case shows the limit concretely, with reflection failing to catch a wrong intermediate estimate that a retrieved near-miss problem exposes immediately. Where it works it is trained rather than prompted and paired with something else: one safety method reduces harmful completions from 13.8 to 4.1 percent, nearly threefold over mainstream approaches, while gaining helpfulness and surviving an adaptive attack without targeted adversarial training. The design caution the corpus states is that rewarding reflection directly invites reward hacking, since an agent can produce reflective text that scores well without changing what it does -- and one reflection-depth sweep is monotone in opposite directions on the two axes it affects, which its authors use to justify keeping reflection shallow.
